newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Bottom fishing underpins Singapore stocks at close.
newsitem.headline: Bottom fishing underpins Singapore stocks at close.

text.p: The Singapore stock market ended firmer on Wednesday, underpinned by bottom-fishing of low-valued stocks and selected blue chips, dealers said.
Total turnover was a robust 149.5 million shares, with 198 gainers to 135 losers.

"People continued to accumulate good traditional blue chip stocks that have been bashed recently," a local dealer said. He also noted keen, selected buying of low-valued electronics stocks amid belief of a second-half recovery for the sector.
The Straits Times Industrials Index improved from its day's low of 2,054.80 to end 12.45 points up, at 2,068.13.
The SES electronics index rose 2.38 points or 1.89 percent to end at a new year high of 128.11.

Multimedia company Creative Technologies led gainers, rising Singapore $1.70 to end at S$24.90 after analysts upgraded its earnings outlook. Singapore Telecommunications, which has fallen 26 percent from its year high, rose S$0.11 to S$2.53 in active trade of about seven million shares.

Disk drive maker MMI was the most active with over 10 million shares and ended S$0.02 up at S$0.75. The low-valued stock benefited from buy recommendations by some broking houses. -- Angela Tan, Singapore newsroom (65 8703083)
